title: Pressure/Flow Switch Stuck Closed
shortDescription: Pressure switch closed when pump is off.
fullDescription:
FL1 indicates the flow/pressure switch is reading closed when the heater pump should be off. Often a stuck switch or wiring short.

Heater is locked out until cleared.

fixSteps.title: Inspect pressure switch
fixSteps.instruction: Locate switch on heater manifold; tap gently and check wiring.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Drain below heater, swap pressure switch, refill.

whenToCallPro: If wiring is damaged or board suspect.

faq.a: No, it is a critical safety device.

title: Low/No Flow Detected
shortDescription: Pressure switch open while pump is running.
fullDescription:
FL2 means the heater is calling for heat and the pump is running, but the pressure switch is not closing. Indicates inadequate flow.

Usually clogged filter, low water, or air lock.

fixSteps.title: Bleed air
fixSteps.instruction: Loosen pump union to release air pocket.

faq.a: Lockout protects it; clear flow first.

title: Water Overheat Detected
fullDescription:
OH appears when water temperature exceeds 108 to 112 F. Spa locks out heater until temperature falls.

Common in hot weather or when cover left on with jets running.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cover, turn off pumps, let cool 30 min.

fixSteps.title: Inspect relay
fixSteps.instruction: If returns, have tech check heater relay.

faq.a: Wait until temperature falls below setpoint.

title: High-Limit Sensor Tripped
fullDescription:
HL means the high-limit thermistor in the heater tube detected unsafe temperature, often from low flow or sensor fault.

Requires resetting and addressing root cause.

faq.a: Yes once cool, but root cause must be fixed.

title: Heater Temperature Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
SN1 indicates the main water temperature sensor is open, shorted, or out of range. Heater is disabled.

Usually a faulty thermistor or bad connection.

fixSteps.title: Reseat plug
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and reconnect sensor at board.

faq.a: Pump still runs in some models.

title: Hi-Limit Sensor Open Circuit
fullDescription:
SN2 means the hi-limit thermistor circuit is open. Heater is locked out for safety.

Replacement of the sensor is typical fix.

title: Water Below Setpoint
fullDescription:
COOL is informational, indicating the spa is more than 20F below setpoint and the heater is running. Not an error unless persistent.

Normal after a fill or extended cover-off.

fixSteps.title: Verify heater
fixSteps.instruction: If after 12h still COOL, suspect element.

title: Freeze Protection Active
fullDescription:
ICE indicates water is below 40F and pumps cycle automatically to prevent freezing. Not an error.

Review insulation and breaker if recurring.

title: Priming Mode Active
fullDescription: PR appears at startup and lasts up to 5 minutes while the system primes pumps. Press Jets to exit early once water flows.

fixSteps.title: Press Jets
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle jet button to confirm flow and exit.

fixSteps.title: Bleed air
fixSteps.instruction: If stuck, loosen pump union briefly.

title: Dry-Fire Detected
fullDescription:
DR indicates the heater detected a dry condition (rapid temperature rise without flow). Heater locks out to prevent element damage.

Must verify water level and prime before resetting.
whenToCallPro: If element damaged from dry fire.

faq.a: Often caught early; replace if reads continuity issue.
